This publication is part of WHO's recommendations on non-clinical interventions to reduce unnecessary cesarean sections. It is made publicly available for transparency and informational purposes, as required by WHO guidelines. The publication includes various interventions to reduce unnecessary cesarean sections, categorized as follows: 1. Educational Interventions: Education of health professionals (10 studies) Education of pregnant women (9 studies) Education of the community (2 studies) 2. Management of Labour Interventions: Continuous support during labor (22 studies) Implementation of intrapartum care guidelines (21 studies) Active management of labor (15 studies) Specific physical ambiance during labor/delivery (5 studies) Systematic X-ray pelvimetry in women with previous cesarean sections (1 study) Non-pharmacological pain relief (1 study) Computer-generated partogram (1 study) 3. Regulatory/Administrative Interventions: Audit and feedback (16 studies) Peer review (10 studies) Goal setting for cesarean rates (4 studies) Mandatory second opinion for cesarean indications (3 studies) Financial incentives (2 studies) Public dissemination of cesarean rates (2 studies) 24-hour in-house physician coverage (1 study) Opinion leaders to encourage guideline use (1 study) 4. Other Interventions: Midwife-led continuity-of-care model (15 studies) Exercise during pregnancy (6 studies) Hospital quality improvement programs (4 studies) The publication is © World Health Organization 2018, with some rights reserved.
